categories.description: Signs that impose a legal obligation on road users.

categories.description: Signs that warn road users of a hazard ahead.
categories.colour: White background with red border and black symbols

categories.description: Signs that provide useful information to road users.
categories.colour: Blue or green background with white text/symbols

placement_rules.general: Signs installed alongside or above roadways/highways.
placement_rules.parking_signs: Fixed at approximately 15 degrees to carriageway.
placement_rules.horizontal_curves: Angle determined by approaching traffic direction.
placement_rules.sign_faces: Normally vertical; tilted on gradients for line-of-sight.
placement_rules.restriction: STOP or GIVE WAY signs must NOT share post with warning signs.

visibility_rules.night_requirement: Cautionary/warning and regulatory signs must be lit or retro-reflective.
visibility_rules.breakdown_requirement: Retro-reflective triangle mandatory behind vehicle during breakdown.

road_markings.title: Road Marking
road_markings.definition: Set of lines and designs painted or installed on road surface to facilitate smooth traffic movement, demarcate parking/no-parking areas, and convey vital information.

colours.use: Kerb and object marking (combined with white or yellow)

types.name: Centre Line — Single Broken
types.description: Separates opposing traffic; vehicles may cross when safe to overtake.

types.name: Centre Line — Single Continuous (Barrier Line)
types.description: Prohibits crossing/overtaking. Vehicles must not cross this line.

types.name: Centre Line — Double Broken
types.description: Separates opposing traffic; overtaking permitted when safe.

types.name: Centre Line — Double with One Continuous
types.description: Mixed: one direction may overtake (broken side), other must not (solid side).

types.name: Lane Lines
types.description: Broken white lines separating same-direction lanes. May change lanes when safe.

types.name: Edge / Border Lines
types.description: Continuous lines at road edges marking safe drivable limit.

types.name: Stop Lines
types.description: White transverse lines at intersections/pedestrian crossings. Vehicles must stop behind.

types.name: Give Way Lines
types.description: Double broken transverse lines indicating yield point.

types.name: Pedestrian Crossing (Zebra Crossing)
types.description: Alternating black and white stripes. Pedestrians must cross here; drivers must yield.

types.name: Parking Prohibited Lines
types.description: Solid continuous yellow line on kerb with No-Parking sign. Indicates no-parking extent.

pedestrians.title: Safety Tips for Pedestrians
rules: Walk on footpath; if unavailable, walk on RIGHT side facing traffic.
Cross only at designated points: zebra crossings, pelican crossings, subways, foot over bridges.
Never assume the driver has seen you before crossing.
Wait for suitable gap in traffic flow before crossing.
Never jump over divider railings.
Always hold children's hands while crossing the road.
Avoid crossing road between parked cars.
Take the shortest and most direct route across.
Use Green Cross Code: STOP → LOOK → LISTEN → THINK → Live.
Extra care required on crests and curves.
Children under 10 must be accompanied by an adult.

cyclists.title: Safety Tips for Cyclist
rules: Keep cycle in working condition: check brakes, tyres, air, bell, light, chain before riding.
Obey traffic signals; give hand signals for turns.
Do not overload; maximum 2 persons on a bicycle.
Move on LEFT side of road.
Avoid overtaking; single file if road is narrow.
No acrobatics; keep both hands on handlebar.
Use only cycle tracks if available.
Remain constantly alert on roads.
Wear bright clothes; have bright front light at night.
Use retro-reflective tapes on cycle for night visibility.

school_bus.title: Safety Tips for School Bus
boarding_rules: Wait till bus stops completely before boarding.
Ensure bag or clothes do not get stuck.
travelling_rules: Be seated properly and face forward.
Do not put any body part outside the bus.
alighting_rules: Be visible to driver while alighting.
Do not crawl under bus to pick up lost things.
Never move behind the bus (driver's blind spot).

parking.title: Know the Correct Way of Parking
rules: Always look for authorised parking.
Opt for parallel parking.
Always use indicators while parking.
While opening car door, ensure it does not bang another car.
In slope/hilly areas: keep forward gear if slope is behind; reverse gear if slope is in front.
Always pull hand brake unless asked by attendant.
Take receipt from parking attendant.
Respect No Standing/No Waiting/No Parking zones.
Do not park haphazardly.
Avoid keeping valuables in parked car.
Never leave children in a parked and locked car.
Park with parking lights on at night.
Avoid parking brawls — it is a form of road rage.

first_aid.title: How to Help Road Crash Victims
remember: Call help and look for unconscious victims.

A.action: Clear the airway — lay victim gently, turn to one side, loosen clothing at neck/chest/waist, tilt face down so tongue falls forward, remove dirt/blood/vomit from mouth.

B.action: Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation if victim not breathing. Blow every 4 seconds (adults), every 3 seconds (children).

C.action: Stop any bleeding — direct pressure with thick pad of bandage/cloth, elevate bleeding limbs, do not remove foreign objects from wound, apply pads and bandage around wound.

mouth_to_mouth_steps: Step 2: Tilt head back, lift chin, check breathing.
Step 5: Position hands in centre of chest.
Step 6: Firmly push down ~2 inches on chest 15 times.
Continue: 2 breaths + 15 chest compressions until help arrives.

supreme_court_ruling.case: Pt. Parmanand Katara vs Union of India
supreme_court_ruling.citation: Criminal Writ Petition No. 270 of 1988, D/-28.8.1989, AIR 1989 Supreme Court 2039
supreme_court_ruling.ruling_summary: Every injured citizen brought for medical treatment must be given immediate medical aid. No legal impediment for a medical professional called to attend an injured person needing immediate assistance. IPC, CrPC, Motor Vehicles Act contain no provisions preventing doctors from promptly attending seriously injured persons before police arrival.

causes.description: Higher speed exponentially multiplies crash risk and injury severity. Faster vehicles need greater braking distance and are more prone to skidding.
Alcohol impairs concentration, slows reaction, dampens fear, incites risk-taking. For every 0.05% rise in BAC, crash risk doubles.
Wrong manner or wrong location overtaking.
Mobile phone use, adjusting mirrors/radio, eating/drinking, animals on road, billboards.
Vehicles crossing intersection without caring for traffic signal.
Failure to use mandated protective equipment.
Not staying in lane; improper overtaking.

rules: Reduce speed.
Turn headlights on LOW BEAM mode.
Turn on fog lamps and parking lights.
Use defroster and windscreen wipers.
Maintain safe distance between vehicles.
If impossible to drive, pull off completely and keep blinkers on.
Experienced and skilled drivers only.
Follow speed limits; reduce speed at turns.
Always give priority to uphill traffic.
Never drive under influence of alcohol on hills.
Do not overtake on turns, curves, or bridges.
Do not overload vehicle.
Avoid clutch pedal on turns and hairpin bends.
Do not run on neutral while driving downhill.
Always blow horn on turns.
Check brakes and tyres before hill journey.
Ensure all headlights, taillights, directional signals operational.
Drive slowly at night.
Keep more space between vehicles.
Use HIGH beam only in dark/remote areas where road is not visible.
On well-lit corridors: drive with low beam (dipped headlights).
Never stop on any roadway at night.
Never drink and drive.
Retro-reflective triangle mandatory during breakdown.
Drive slow.
Keep pedalling brakes to check performance.
Use windscreen wipers and demisters.
Increase distance between vehicles.
Do not take sharp turns.
If heavy rain: keep blinkers on.
Drive carefully through waterlogged roads (potholes).
If no power brakes: drive more cautiously and slowly.
Do not overtake unnecessarily.
Ensure tyres properly maintained — clean and visible treads.
Do not speed up through collected water (splash hazard).
Keep mud flaps in good condition.
Always keep umbrella in vehicle during monsoon.

myths_vs_facts.myth: The lane in front of your home is meant for you to play.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Definitely not. It can lead to crashes and injury. It is only meant for traffic.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Children are allowed to ride a light scooter on roads inside a colony.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Not so. It is illegal on any road where traffic is plying.

myths_vs_facts.myth: It is alright for 2 adults and 1 child to ride a two-wheeler.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Definitely not. Only 2 persons can ride a two-wheeler, both wearing helmets.

myths_vs_facts.myth: One can answer an urgent mobile call while driving.
myths_vs_facts.fact: No. Use of mobile phone while driving can lead to accidents and is a punishable offence.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Helmet not necessary while riding two-wheeler for short distances.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Helmet must always be worn, even for shorter distances. Many crashes occur during short rides.
